feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so I state no outcome for it. The best raced design is iteration 3 (score 893.56): base_speed 1.2, sensors at ±3 cm, kp 2.25, kd 0.9. It finished the oval 20/20 and the s-bend 20/20, and the slalom 15/20. Its slalom failures were all off-track (5 of 20), with slalom steering_oscillation of 0.25 and rms_error of 0.012 m. Iteration 4 cut base_speed to 1.1 and scored 879.5, with the slalom worse (13/20 finished, 7 off-track). Speed is therefore not the cause of the slalom failures, and base_speed 1.2 is correct.

The candidate is valid and well reasoned. The spread widens to ±4 cm with 16 mm sensors, which are in range. The weights stay at -2..2. The gains are rescaled to keep the per-cm response: kp 2.25 to 3.0 gives 2.25×(2/3) ≈ 1.5 per cm, now 3.0×0.5 = 1.5, and kd 0.9 to 1.2 gives 0.6 per cm, which holds. The change is single-axis (sensor spread, with gain compensation), so the race should isolate the line-loss mechanism. Oval and s-bend should stay near iteration 3, since the per-cm gain is unchanged.

Read the race this way. If slalom line_loss_events fall and slalom finishes rise above 17/20 with the mean above 893, keep this design and consider a small base_speed rise (1.2 to 1.25) to recover completion time. If slalom off-track events persist while line_loss_events are low and max_error is high, the cause is overshoot on tight bends, not line loss. Then the next step is more kd (toward 1.4), or a slightly lower kp (toward 2.6), not more speed cuts. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 on any track, the larger kp and kd are too aggressive for the wider spread, so return kd toward 1.0 and keep kp at 3.0.
requested_changes: If slalom off-track failures persist with line_loss_events below 0.25 (overshoot rather than line loss): raise controller.kd from 1.2 toward 1.4 with kp 3.0 held, because iteration 3 slalom oscillation was 0.25 and the failures came from drift on sharp bends.

If steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 on any track: lower controller.kd from 1.2 toward 1.0 and keep kp at 3.0, so the rescaled gains do not add jitter on the wider spread (iteration 3 oscillation was 0.21 to 0.28).

If the slalom finishes cleanly with completion_time under 2.8 s: keep the geometry and gains, and raise controller.base_speed from 1.2 to 1.25 in one step to recover time, since iteration 3 slalom mean finish time was 2.43 s and the oval/s-bend finish times were 2.04 s and 2.25 s.
